doc.title: Phil Flanigan interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: Moving to Florida and living there
summary: Asked for anything else, he sums up leaving New York for Florida eight years ago.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Well I want to thank you for joining us here. Anything I haven’t asked you about that you’d like to throw in there on your own?

I can’t really say that — I thought we were going to go a little bit more into history — I guess you have my basic history about going to New York and all that stuff, and then pretty much I left New York for Florida, I guess that was eight years ago, and since then I’ve been trying to be able to live in Florida and have my arms reach out further into the environment rather than, in New York, you don’t need a very long arm, there’s people real close.
So you have to travel quite a bit to get out and get the work.
Yeah. But that’s okay. Florida is pretty flat and boring. I like looking at the hills and stuff here.
Yeah. A different change of scenery.
Florida, especially in the summer, can be brutal.
